text:
anne-devex: Heads-up — onboarding sample app is noisy and we lose request IDs across retries. Steps to repro in sandbox.
anne-devex: Quick logs:
```
INFO 2026-03-23T12:00:01Z fetch /v1/predict body=...
ERROR 2026-03-23T12:00:02Z retry attempt=1 code=503 message=upstream timeout
INFO 2026-03-23T12:00:03Z fetch /v1/predict body=...
```
anne-devex: None of the ERROR lines include req_id or traceparent. Makes correlating failures impossible.
sam-telemetry: ugh. which SDK/version? node or python sample app?
kai-eng: probably Node sampleapp. We saw an autoinit hook ordering quirk: logging hooks run before OTEL context is attached -> reqid not propagated into logs on retry.
anne-devex: yes node 0.9.2 sampleapp. Starting with `npm start --sample=quickstart`.
sam-telemetry: can you paste the minimal repro env/flags? do you have OTEL envs set?
anne-devex: env: `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info`, `REDWOOD_USE_OTEL=true`, no manual traceprop headers in sample. Also using our retry middleware (auth+retry) in front.
kai-eng: that matches. Our Node SDK autoinit does: 1) configure logger 2) init retry middleware 3) register OTEL hook. If logger captures request id from process-local storage before OTEL hook attaches, logs miss reqid for subsequent async retries.
sam-telemetry: workaround: set OTEL hooks to init earlier via env `REDWOOD_OTEL_PREINIT=true` or manual init in app entrypoint: `await telemetry.init()` before logger setup.
anne-devex: tried that — calling `telemetry.init()` early fixes the reqid for the first request but retry paths still sometimes lose it (race on middleware wrap).
kai-eng: can you paste the retry stack snippet? maybe middleware re-wraps the request in a new async context.
anne-devex: snippet:
```
// retry-middleware.js
async function callWithRetry(req) {
  try {
    return await backend.call(req);
  } catch (e) {
    await sleep(100);
    // re-fetch without preserving context?
    return await backend.call(req);
  }
}
```
anne-devex: looks like we're creating new async boundaries without reattaching context.
sam-telemetry: yep. Two options: 1) update retry-middleware to propagate OTEL context/reqid using `telemetry.runInSpan(...)` or `tracer.withSpan(...)` 2) have logger read reqid from header fallback (extract traceparent from outgoing request and attach to logs).
anne-devex: what's the recommended DX fix? We want minimal friction for new users and parity with python SDK which seems fine.
kai-eng: python SDK sets OTEL hooks earlier in autoinit; Node's boot order is fixable in 0.9.3 but we should also add a small helper in sampleapp README: "If you rely on retries, call `await telemetry.bootstrap()` before creating your logger or using retry middleware."
sam-telemetry: also add a defensive server-side guard: when emitting logs, if req_id missing, try to read `traceparent` from request headers and set req_id temporarily. That helps customers who can't change middleware immediately.
anne-devex: agree. I'll open PR for sampleapp doc + small guard in logger. Also filing a runtime bug for SDK autoinit ordering.
infra-bot: @anne-devex created ticket INFRA-1256: "node sdk: telemetry autoinit ordering causes missing reqid on retries" :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded to sandbox in 42s (build 2026.3.227) :white_check_mark:
kai-eng: one more thing: we should add an example in devex quickstart showing `export OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,baggage` and `export REDWOOD_LOG_FORMAT=structured` so folks can correlate quickly.
anne-devex: done. I'll also add a tiny test in sampleapp that simulates a retry and asserts reqid present in all log lines.
sam-telemetry: thanks — once PRs land we'll backport a patch to 0.9.x and ship in 0.10.0 with release notes about "Telemetry: ensure logger hooks attach after OTEL init to preserve request IDs across retries"
anne-devex: great, thanks y'all :rocket:
